summary: Boyd Michailovsky works in linguistics and Tibetology. He held positions at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1976–1978) and Langues et civilisations à tradition orale (attested 1990).

Brad Warner works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Kent State University and under Tim McCarthy, Gyomay Kubose, and Gudō Wafu Nishijima. In 2007, he led Dogen Sangha International, and he founded Dogen Sangha Los Angeles in 2012.

Bradford Lyman Phillips works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Naropa University, Harvard University (M.T.S., 1993), and the University of Virginia (B.A., 1989; Ph.D., 2004) under David F. Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, Michael Aris, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies and philosophy. His career includes posts as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad and excavation under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich. He held posts at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, SOAS, and the University of Munich.
Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015) under the supervision of Patrick Arthur Pranke.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the University of Calcutta and SOAS (Ph.D. under Arthur Llewellyn Basham), and also attended Cambridge. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan S. Gillon works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1980–1984) and served as an Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University (~1992).

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Vanderbilt and Kyoto University. He taught at Shiga and Kwansei Gakuin universities, held research fellowships at Kyoto and Otani, and taught philosophy at Loyola University Maryland.
Brian Bocking is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and studied under Ngawang Wangyal.

Brian D. Ruppert specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Willis Stoesz, he held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) before joining Bates College (~2018) as Kazushige Hirasawa Professor and Asian Studies Chair.

Brian Daizen Victoria specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. Educated at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, Eihei-ji, and Temple University, he held posts at Auckland, Adelaide, Antioch, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Indiana University in 2005 under the doctoral supervision of György Kara.

Brian Houghton Hodgson was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at East India Company College and Fort William College, he served in Nepal as Assistant Resident (1820) and British Resident (~1833–1843).

Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned a PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein.

Bridget Allchin was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. Educated at Cape Town and UCL, she was a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1978–2017) and held leadership roles in the Ancient India & Iran Trust and the EASAA.
Brigitte Marschall earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna, where she became a professor around 1999.
Brigitte Steinmann is a scholar in Tibetology. She studied under Alexander W. Macdonald and traditional teacher Bahadur Singh, and held a post at the University of Montpellier (attested 2004).
